title: California's 19th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 19th Congressional District pits incumbent Democrat Jimmy Panetta against Republican challenger Peter Coe Verbica. The district spans California's Central Coast, including portions of Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Monterey, and San Luis Obispo counties. Panetta, first elected in 2016, is seeking a fifth term in Congress and represents a district that has been held by Democrats without interruption since 1977. The Cook Political Report rated this race as 'Solidly Democratic' ahead of the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, in which Panetta won 58.6% of the vote and Verbica advanced with 20.4%.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election in California's 19th Congressional District. The Cook Political Report rated the race as Solidly Democratic prior to the primary.

candidates.name: Jimmy Panetta
candidates.summary: Jimmy Panetta is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 19th Congressional District, first elected in 2016. He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the House Budget Committee, and previously served as a deputy district attorney and as a Navy Reserve intelligence officer deployed to Afghanistan, where he was awarded a Bronze Star. Panetta is the son of former U.S. Defense Secretary and CIA Director Leon Panetta, who previously represented the same region in Congress.

candidates.name: Peter Coe Verbica
candidates.summary: Peter Coe Verbica is a certified financial planner and Managing Director at Silicon Private Wealth, running as a Republican challenger for California's 19th Congressional District. He holds a JD from Santa Clara University School of Law, an MS in Real Estate Development from MIT, and previously ran for the California Board of Equalization in 2022, advancing to the top-two general election. Verbica has served as Chair of the Santa Cruz County Republican Central Committee and as president of the California Congress of Republicans, and his campaign focuses on restoring affordability, cutting taxes, improving water infrastructure, and reforming immigration.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling is available, which limits confidence. However, the available race data strongly favors Democrats: incumbent Jimmy Panetta has held the seat since 2016; Democrats have held the district continuously since 1977; Cook Political Report rated the race Solidly Democratic ahead of the primary; and Panetta won the top-two primary convincingly with 58.6% of the vote while Republican challenger Peter Coe Verbica advanced with only 20.4%. These structural and electoral factors indicate an overwhelming Democratic advantage despite the absence of polling.
